questions.q: You want to copy files quickly to an external USB drive. Which port on the Raspberry Pi 5 is the best choice?
choices: A black USB 2.0 port, because it works with any device
The USB-C port on the bottom edge
A blue USB 3.0 port, because it transfers data much faster
The Ethernet port, because it runs at 1 Gbps
questions.explain: The blue USB 3.0 ports are about ten times faster than the black USB 2.0 ports for data transfer, making them the right choice for a fast drive. The USB-C port on the Pi 5 is power-only and cannot transfer data at all.

questions.q: What happens if you use a standard phone charger instead of the supplied 27 W power supply with the Raspberry Pi 5?
choices: The Pi will not turn on at all
The Pi will display a yellow lightning bolt warning and slow itself down
The Pi will run normally but the Active Cooler will not work
The Pi will start a backup shutdown to protect its files
questions.explain: A phone charger cannot supply enough current, causing the voltage to drop. The Pi responds by showing a yellow lightning bolt icon and throttling the processor to use less power, making it run noticeably slower. It will still turn on, so option 0 is wrong.

questions.q: Which part of the Raspberry Pi 5 acts as the computer's short-term memory, holding whatever it is working on right now — and is completely cleared every time you switch the power off?
choices: The microSD card, which stores all running programs
The SoC (BCM2712 chip), which processes and remembers all current tasks
The RAM (16 GB LPDDR4X), which is fast but volatile
The RTC battery, which keeps data alive when the power is removed
questions.explain: RAM is the Pi's fast, temporary workspace — it holds whatever is being processed right now, but loses everything the moment power is cut. The microSD card is long-term storage (it keeps files after power off); the SoC is the processor, not memory; and the RTC battery only keeps the clock ticking, not your data.

questions.q: The Raspberry Pi 5 has two micro-HDMI ports. If you are connecting a single monitor for the first time, which port should you use?
choices: Port 1, the one closer to the USB-C power socket
Either port — they behave identically for a single monitor
The DSI port, which is designed for display output
Port 0, the one nearer the centre of the board
questions.explain: The chapter states you should always use micro-HDMI port 0 for a single monitor. Port 0 is the one closer to the centre of the board. DSI is a completely different connector used only for the official Pi Touchscreen ribbon cable.

questions.q: What is the correct order for connecting a Raspberry Pi 5 for the very first time?
choices: Plug in the power first so the Pi is ready to detect devices as you connect them
Connect the monitor, keyboard, and mouse first, then plug in power last
Connect the microSD card last, after the Pi has booted, so it mounts cleanly
It does not matter — you can connect everything in any order
questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: connect all peripherals (monitor, keyboard, mouse, network cable) before applying power. Plugging in a monitor after the Pi has booted can result in the display not being detected and a blank screen appearing.
